claims.claim: A packaged AlGaN/GaN Hall-effect sensor module was fabricated, packaged (LCC package, Al wire bonds, EPO-TEK 353ND, 150°C vacuum bake, zirconia holder, graphite shield), and deployed in-vessel near the HSX stellarator plasma edge during the August 2025 campaign, producing shot-resolved voltage transients with clear ignition/discharge dynamics and a qualitative temporal correlation with diamagnetic-loop stored energy across three discharge classes (raw scope traces for representative shots, e.g. main-coil-current logs for shots 65 and 68, plus stored-energy .dat files for shots #18/#19/#20, exist in the raw archive).

claims.limitation: The quantitative correlation with diamagnetic-loop stored energy is currently qualitative only (no correlation coefficient computed as of the cited audit); the sensor output is voltage-domain, not a calibrated field measurement (see C06). No temperature log exists for the sensor during these shots.

claims.claim: On a bench resistor-ring emulator (4×680Ω ring + 2.2kΩ across p1–p2, 20 mA bias, 20 kHz current-spinning, gain 100.3), current-spinning demodulation collapsed a 686 mV raw offset to ≤ 5 mV — a suppression of ≥130× (limited by the oscilloscope's 8-bit quantization over 5 cycles). This is explicitly readout-architecture validation on an emulator, not a measurement of the real GaN Hall die's offset.

claims.claim: Mutual/cross-calibration between the Hall and coil channels is direction-dependent and only partly feasible, not a symmetric "the sensors calibrate each other" relationship. Hall→coil correction of the coil chain's integrator drift/leakage/initial condition is the only hardware-proven direction (demonstrated outside fusion in a CERN bench context and deployed at ITER's OVSS system, per the corpus's cited sources). Coil→Hall is only conditionally feasible, and only for gain (via a trusted coil chain plus real field excursions); the coil can never deliver the Hall offset, because a constant Hall offset is observationally identical to a static field shift the coil cannot see — offset recovery requires zero-field (or known-field) epochs or an external absolute reference. If both Hall and coil parameters drift simultaneously and unreferenced, the pair has a proven two-parameter blind spot: it can detect that the two channels disagree but cannot attribute which channel drifted.
claims.opt2_mapping: Opt2 Element 2: integrate Hall + inductive coils as a hybrid diagnostic (mutual-consistency claim, kept distinct from absolute calibration C06, bandwidth fusion C08, and radiation compensation C09)
claims.limitation: This is a structural-identifiability derivation (a proof-style result, labeled Derived/Inferred by the source document itself), not an experimental result; the source states explicitly "no hardware demonstration of the coil→Hall direction exists in fusion conditions," and the one real-world coil→Hall gain-tracking precedent it cites is a single non-fusion, unirradiated, driven-ramp source. Mutual agreement between the two channels is explicitly NOT automatic absolute calibration per this source; it can at most indicate that the channels have drifted apart, without identifying which one moved. Folder 08 (the source mission) has not passed its own redteam/synthesis stages.

claims.claim: The proposed hybrid architecture treats bandwidth fusion as a distinct design element from calibration: the Hall channel is proposed to supply the DC/low-frequency field content the coil cannot see (the coil measures dB/dt and is blind at steady field), while an embedded calibration-winding injection scheme is proposed to be placed in an "overlap band" — above the drift band, below the Hall sensor's dynamic pole, and inside the coil's flat response — so that injecting near/above the Hall pole can identify Hall dynamics (pole/delay) that neither channel could establish alone at low frequency.
claims.opt2_mapping: Opt2 Element 2: integrate Hall + inductive coils as a hybrid diagnostic (bandwidth-fusion claim, kept distinct from absolute calibration C06, mutual consistency C07, and radiation compensation C09)
claims.page_or_section: §1 ("Hall → coil" bullet, "it supplies the DC/low-frequency field the coil cannot see"); frequency-plan detail in sources/phd/P/01/08_Hall_Coil_Hybrid_Radiation_Strategy_2026-07/outputs/03_RADIATION_COMPENSATION_ARCHITECTURE.md §5.2 ("Frequency plan and lock-in detection")
claims.limitation: No bandwidth-fusion hardware test has been run; the design depends on an as-yet-unverified Hall readout bandwidth (see C05 — the manuscript's own 1 MHz figure is undocumented) and on a machine-EMI survey that has not been performed. The source document labels every item in this section "Derived" design rules, not observed results.

claims.claim: A layered "anchored hybrid" architecture (machine-current/vacuum-field anchor epochs + zero-field offset epochs + optional embedded-winding online gain tracking + a top-tier material-diverse witness Hall die) is proposed to separate temperature-driven from radiation-driven sensor drift and to compensate for it, with radiation qualification work (Phase 4 / tiers T3) explicitly collaborator-led, never on the HSX critical path, and never claimed as an experimental result in first-author work. The corpus states plainly that the GaN/AlGaN radiation-drift magnitude is currently Unknown: no GaN or AlGaN Hall-plate neutron dataset exists in the literature reviewed.

Folder 08 has no redteam/synthesis pass yet (per the B00 inventory handoff note), so this framing is pre-adversarial-review within the corpus's own process.
